summary.text: The contractor tender closed on 20 November with only two bids. The team had hoped for at least four.

quotes.text: The contractor tender closed on the twentieth of November and we only got two bids, we were hoping for at least four.

summary.text: Procurement accepts two bids as the minimum, so the tender is compliant. Ravi flagged that two bids are a problem for value for money because there are too few prices to compare.

quotes.text: Procurement said two is the minimum they accept, so we're compliant, but it's a problem for value for money.
With only two, you can't really tell where the middle of uh the market is.

summary.text: Kemlite Builders bid £310k (three hundred and ten thousand) and the other bid was £345k (three hundred and forty-five thousand), so Kemlite was the lower bid.

quotes.text: Kemlite Builders came in at three hundred and ten thousand, the other bid was three hundred and forty five.
Kemlite is the lower one, correct.

summary.text: Jonas asked whether the two bids were priced on the same basis. Ravi said he would need to check the detail before answering. The board agreed the field is thin but compliant.

quotes.text: I'd want to check the detail before I answered that properly.
It's thin, we've said that, and it's compliant, we've said that.

topics.title: End stage report and stage 3 approval

summary.text: The end stage report recommends awarding the contract to Kemlite and moving into stage 3, construction.

quotes.text: The end stage report recommends we award to Kemlite and move into stage three, construction.

summary.text: From the user side, Kemlite's design met all the must-haves. The other, higher bid dropped the second meeting room, which made the choice clearer.

quotes.text: From the user side the Kemlite design met all our must-haves, the other one dropped the second meeting room.
It means the two bids aren't as hard to choose between as I'd feared.

summary.text: The board approved stage 3 and the award to Kemlite Builders at £310k. Jonas and Wei Ling both agreed.

quotes.text: the board approves stage three and the award to Kemlite Builders at three hundred and ten thousand.

actions.text: Issue the letter of award to Kemlite Builders.

quotes.text: I'll issue the letter of award tomorrow.

summary.text: The workstation supplier is now quoting a 10-week lead time, up from 6 weeks. This came in after the meeting papers went out, so it is not in the report.

quotes.text: The workstation supplier is quoting ten weeks lead time now, sort of it used to be six.
It came through to me, I think, after the pack went out, so it's not in the report.

summary.text: If the 10 weeks holds, there is a real but uncertain chance that the desks arrive after the move-in date.

quotes.text: If that holds, there's a real chance the desks arrive after the move-in date.
It's a real chance, it isn't certain.

summary.text: The standard desks could be ordered now, with only the meeting room tables ordered later. Grace did not want to decide this in the meeting, so the question was left open.

quotes.text: We can order the standard desks now and only sort of the meeting room tables later.
Though I don't want to rush into a decision on it here, I'd rather hear I mean a bit more first.

actions.text: Forward the workstation supplier's quote to Ravi so the 10-week lead time is in writing.

quotes.text: Way Ling, could you send me the quote, so I have the sort of ten weeks in writing?
I'll forward it, it's in my inbox.

summary.text: The January network install needs the central IT team, who are also committed to another project that month.

quotes.text: The network install in January needs the central IT team, and uh they're also committed to another project that month.

summary.text: The install can only happen if central IT gives the team the second and third weeks of January together. This has been discussed with central IT but nothing is agreed yet.

quotes.text: So our install can kind of only happen if central IT gives us the second and third week of January.
We've talked to them, but nothing's been agreed.

summary.text: Nobody knows how firm central IT's other commitment is or whether it overlaps the same weeks.

quotes.text: So I can't say whether it overlaps exactly or only partly.

actions.text: Raise the need for central IT's second and third weeks of January with the IT director.

quotes.text: I'll raise it with the IT director at the leadership meeting on Thursday.

summary.text: The schedule is built on the landlord approving the works by 13 December.

quotes.text: Our schedule is built on the landlord approving the works by the thirteenth of December.

summary.text: The landlord has been asked but has not replied, so the team keeps assuming the 13 December date.

quotes.text: They haven't said no, they just haven't replied, so for now we kind of keep assuming the thirteenth.
They've been asked. It's with uh them. They haven't come back.

summary.text: The meeting closed with the team carrying on with 13 December as the planned date and continuing to chase the landlord.

quotes.text: On the landlord, we keep going on the thirteenth and keep chasing.

actions.text: Keep chasing the landlord for approval and tell Grace early if the date slips.

quotes.text: Okay, keep chasing them, and tell me early if it slips.
Understood.
